chunks: Hadith 3467 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who made a slave of his a mudabbar, and he was a merchant of means. Then the mudabbar bought a bondwoman by the order of his master, and she bore him children. Then the mudabbar died before his master.

He عليه السلام said: “I hold that all that the mudabbar left behind of goods or estates belongs to the one who made him mudabbar. And I hold that the mother of his child remains a slave belonging to the one who made him mudabbar. And I hold that her children are mudabbar in the same state as their father; so when the one who made their father mudabbar dies, they are free.”

key_terms.أَحْرَارٌ: Freed persons, no longer in bondage.
key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدِهِ: The mother of his child, referring here to the bondwoman who bore him children.
key_terms.ٱلْمُدَبَّرُ: A slave designated to be freed upon the death of his master.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the property, bondwoman, and children of a mudabbar slave who dies before his master?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the effects of tadbir when a mudabbar slave acquires property and has children from a bondwoman with the master's permission. It states that the mudabbar’s estate returns to the original master, the bondwoman remains his property, and the children share their father’s mudabbar status and become free upon the death of the original master.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3467 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), about a man who made his wealthy slave mudabbar (to be freed after his death). The mudabbar, with the permission of his master, bought a bondwoman who bore him children. Then the mudabbar died before his master.

Imam (as) said: "I believe that all the property, possessions, or estates left by the mudabbar belong to the one who made him mudabbar. As for the mother of his children, she remains a slave to the one who made him mudabbar. However, I see that her children take the same status as their father-they are mudabbar. Therefore, when the one who made their father mudabbar dies, they will be freed."
